ap_macroeconomics-m01.stem: The dollar depreciates against other currencies. Which statement best explains the effect on net exports of the United States?

options.text: Exports rise and imports fall, because goods made in the United States cost less abroad and imports cost more at home.
options.why: A weaker dollar lowers the foreign price of domestic goods and raises the dollar price of imports.

options.text: Exports fall and net exports fall, because goods made in the United States become more expensive for foreign buyers.
options.why: A depreciation makes domestic goods cheaper abroad.

options.text: Net exports do not change, because trade depends only on incomes and not on the prices of traded goods.
options.why: Relative prices expressed in a common currency affect trade.

options.text: Imports rise and net exports fall, because foreign goods become cheaper for domestic buyers.
options.why: A depreciation makes imports more expensive.

options.text: Exports fall because the dollar is worth less, so fewer foreign buyers want to buy goods made at home.
options.why: A lower-valued dollar makes exports easier to sell.

facts: variant=The dollar depreciates against other cur

ap_macroeconomics-m01.stem: The dollar appreciates against other currencies. Which statement best explains the effect on net exports of the United States?

options.text: Net exports do not change, because exchange rates affect only financial flows and not the prices of traded goods.
options.why: Prices of traded goods change with the exchange rate.

options.text: Exports rise and net exports rise, because goods made in the United States become cheaper for foreign buyers.
options.why: An appreciation makes domestic goods more expensive abroad.

options.text: Exports rise because the dollar is worth more, so more foreign buyers want to buy goods made at home.
options.why: A higher-valued dollar makes exports harder to sell.

options.text: Imports fall and net exports rise, because foreign goods become more expensive for domestic buyers.
options.why: An appreciation makes imports cheaper.

options.text: Exports fall and imports rise, because goods made in the United States cost more abroad and imports cost less at home.
options.why: A stronger dollar raises the foreign price of domestic goods and lowers the dollar price of imports.

facts: variant=The dollar appreciates against other cur
